The results indicate that the Li+ diffusion co­ efficients of the In-doped samples are higher than those of the undoped samples, consistent with their higher ionic conductivity results. This phenomenon may be attributed to severe interfacial side reactions be­ tween undoped LPSC and NCM811, which are effectively suppressed by In doping. (c) S 2p, (d) P 2p XPS spectra of the LPSC-In0.08 after 200 cycles. 131.66 and 132.76 eV correspond to PS4 3−, those at 133.31 and 133.85 eV to P2Sx species, and the peaks at 133.85 and 134.75 eV are assigned to phosphorus oxides (POx). Notably, the relative peak areas of P2Sx and POx are significantly lower in LPSC-In0.08 than in pristine LPSC, further confirming the mitigated interfacial side reactions enabled by In doping. Additionally, the In 3d spectrum of LPSC-In0.08 show no detectable changes after cycling, suggesting that In maintains a stable valence state and does not participate in detrimental interfacial redox processes.
